subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 new action revisions as one grouped security-sensitive update after exact-head checks complete, or require the credential-bearing and Codex Action updates to be reviewed separately?
rationale: The patch changes third-party executable code across workflows with secrets and publishing authority; source inspection found no definite defect, but automation cannot decide whether the grouped supply-chain change matches the repository's accepted trust boundary.

options.title: Approve grouped update after gates
options.body: Rebase once, require all exact-head workflow/security checks to pass, review the upstream revisions, and approve the grouped full-SHA update.

options.title: Split sensitive actions
options.body: Separate Codex Action, token-generation, registry-login, labeling, and stale-action updates into focused PRs for narrower security review.

options.title: Pause for Dependabot refresh
options.body: Leave the PR open until Dependabot can access the repository and produce a stable rebased head with completed checks.

recommendation.title: Approve grouped update after gates
recommendation.body: Rebase once, require all exact-head workflow/security checks to pass, review the upstream revisions, and approve the grouped full-SHA update.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent release-workflow history and direct subscription make this the strongest available owner signal for accepting the grouped automation trust change.
